metadata.description: Name of the Log Analytics workspace that Microsoft Sentinel is enabled on.

properties.description:
A diagnostic setting was deleted from an Azure resource. Diagnostic settings are what send a resource's logs to the workspace, so removing one stops the evidence for that resource (a key vault, a storage account, a firewall) from being collected.

False positives: Infrastructure as code that replaces a setting by deleting and recreating it, and resources being decommissioned.

Response: Recreate the setting, then look at what the same caller did around that time; the deletion is usually preparation for something else.

MITRE ATT&CK sub-techniques: T1562.008.

Source: SentinelWork rule AZ-001.
properties.query:
let AllowedCallers = dynamic([]);
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where ingestion_time() > ago(65m) and ingestion_time() <= ago(5m)
| where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.INSIGHTS/DIAGNOSTICSETTINGS/DELETE"
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ "Success"
| where Caller !in~ (AllowedCallers)
| summarize Deletions = dcount(_ResourceId),
            Resources = make_set(_ResourceId, 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Caller, CallerIpAddress, SubscriptionId
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, Caller, CallerIpAddress, SubscriptionId, Deletions, ResourceId = tostring(Resources[0]),
          Resources

properties.displayName: Owner or other privileged Azure role assigned
properties.description:
Someone assigned Owner, User Access Administrator, Role Based Access Control Administrator or Contributor on an Azure scope. The first three can grant any other role, so a new assignment is both an escalation and a way back in after the original account is cleaned up.

False positives: Planned access changes, new subscriptions, and Privileged Identity Management activating a role (the caller is then the PIM service).

Response: Look up PrincipalId in Entra ID and confirm the assignment with the caller. If it was not approved, remove it and review everything the caller and the principal did since.

MITRE ATT&CK sub-techniques: T1098.003.

Source: SentinelWork rule AZ-002.
properties.query:
let PrivilegedRoleIds = dynamic({
    "8e3af657-a8ff-443c-a75c-2fe8c4bcb635": "Owner",
    "18d7d88d-d35e-4fb5-a5c3-7773c20a72d9": "User Access Administrator",
    "f58310d9-a9f6-439a-9e8d-f62e7b41a168": "Role Based Access Control Administrator",
    "b24988ac-6180-42a0-ab88-20f7382dd24c": "Contributor"});
let AllowedCallers = dynamic([]);
let Succeeded = AzureActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
    | where ingestion_time() > ago(65m) and ingestion_time() <= ago(5m)
    | where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.AUTHORIZATION/ROLEASSIGNMENTS/WRITE"
    | where ActivityStatusValue =~ "Success"
    | distinct CorrelationId, _ResourceId;
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(3h)
| where OperationNameValue =~ "MICROSOFT.AUTHORIZATION/ROLEASSIGNMENTS/WRITE"
| where ActivityStatusValue =~ "Start"
| join kind=inner Succeeded on CorrelationId, _ResourceId
| where Caller !in~ (AllowedCallers)
| extend Request = coalesce(tostring(Properties_d), Properties)
| extend RoleDefinitionId = tolower(extract(@"(?i)roleDefinitions/([0-9a-f\-]{36})", 1, Request)),
         PrincipalId = extract(@"(?i)principalId\W+([0-9a-f\-]{36})", 1, Request),
         PrincipalType = extract(@"(?i)principalType\W+(\w+)", 1, Request)
| extend RoleName = tostring(PrivilegedRoleIds[RoleDefinitionId])
| where isnotempty(RoleName)
| extend Scope = tostring(split(tolower(_ResourceId), "/providers/microsoft.authorization/roleassignments")[0])
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, CallerIpAddress, RoleName, PrincipalId, PrincipalType, Scope, SubscriptionId,
          ResourceGroup, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: Many Azure resources deleted by one caller
properties.description:
One caller deleted an unusually large number of Azure resources within two hours, counted across all subscriptions and addresses the caller used. A compromised administrator or a leaked service principal secret can destroy an environment this way, and it is also what an expensive mistake in a script looks like while it is still running.

False positives: Tearing down a test environment, a pipeline that recreates resources, and clean-up after a project ends.

Response: Contact the caller at once. If the deletion is not theirs, disable the identity, remove its role assignments and begin recovery (soft delete and backups) while the retention lasts.

Source: SentinelWork rule AZ-003.
properties.query:
let MinResources = 20;
let AllowedCallers = dynamic([]);
let Touched = AzureActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
    | where ingestion_time() > ago(65m) and ingestion_time() <= ago(5m)
    | where OperationNameValue endswith "/DELETE" and ActivityStatusValue =~ "Success"
    | distinct Caller;
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where OperationNameValue endswith "/DELETE" and ActivityStatusValue =~ "Success"
| where OperationNameValue !startswith "MICROSOFT.RESOURCES/DEPLOYMENTS"
    and OperationNameValue !startswith "MICROSOFT.AUTHORIZATION/"
    and OperationNameValue !startswith "MICROSOFT.RESOURCES/TAGS"
| where Caller in (Touched) and Caller !in~ (AllowedCallers)
| summarize DeletedResources = dcount(_ResourceId),
            ResourceTypes = make_set(OperationNameValue, 15),
            ResourceGroups = strcat_array(make_set(ResourceGroup, 15), ", "),
            Subscriptions = strcat_array(make_set(SubscriptionId, 10), ", "),
            ResourceSample = make_set(_ResourceId, 15),
            CallerIpAddress = take_any(CallerIpAddress),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Caller
| where DeletedResources >= MinResources
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, Caller, CallerIpAddress, Subscriptions, DeletedResources, ResourceGroups,
          ResourceTypes, ResourceSample

properties.displayName: Run Command executed on a virtual machine
properties.description:
Someone used the Azure Run Command feature to execute a script inside a virtual machine or Arc-enabled server. The script runs as SYSTEM or root and needs no network path or credentials for the machine, only an Azure role, which makes it a favourite way to move from a compromised cloud identity onto servers.

False positives: Operations teams and automation that use Run Command for maintenance.

Response: Ask the caller what was run. The activity log does not contain the script; collect it from the machine (the Run Command extension folder) and from endpoint telemetry at that time.

Source: SentinelWork rule AZ-004.
properties.query:
let AllowedCallers = dynamic([]);
AzureActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where ingestion_time() > ago(65m) and ingestion_time() <= ago(5m)
| where OperationNameValue in~ ("MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/RUNCOMMAND/ACTION",
                                "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINES/RUNCOMMANDS/WRITE",
                                "MICROSOFT.COMPUTE/VIRTUALMACHINESCALESETS/VIRTUALMACHINES/RUNCOMMAND/ACTION",
                                "MICROSOFT.HYBRIDCOMPUTE/MACHINES/RUNCOMMANDS/WRITE")
| where ActivityStatusValue in~ ("Start", "Accept", "Success")
| where Caller !in~ (AllowedCallers)
| summarize Invocations = dcount(CorrelationId),
            Statuses = make_set(ActivityStatusValue, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId = _ResourceId, ResourceGroup, SubscriptionId,
               Operation = OperationNameValue
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, Caller, CallerIpAddress, ResourceId, ResourceGroup, SubscriptionId, Operation,
          Invocations, Statuses
